answer: Shared-pattern overlap audit stops alias farming. The system maps which aliases take the same jobs at the same hours, and an alias pair that overlaps on more than 70 percent of its jobs in 10 epochs gets flagged for review. A flagged alias must pass a violet field check, an opal inventory count, and a wander route log within 48 hours, each filed separately. A confirmed copy loses that epoch pay and sits out for 12 epochs, while the checker who proves the overlap earns a 12 percent bonus on the next job. One operator cannot hide many aliases when their work patterns line up.
